interpretive.rule: 'Unfair' standard tethered to antitrust/statutory policy; UCL independent of predicate statutes — borrowed violations each independently support UCL unlawful prong
Prop 64 standing: 'lost money or property as a result of' satisfied by any concrete economic loss from the UCL violation; reliance required for fraudulent prong
UCL monetary remedy limited to restitution (returning money taken from THIS plaintiff); non-restitutionary disgorgement of defendant's total profits not available to private plaintiffs

operational_notes_for_steward_cases.ucl_pleading_strategy: In every California consumer fraud case, the UCL claim is the overlay. Plead UCL unlawful prong borrowing each specific statute violated (CLRA, Rees-Levering, Rosenthal, FDCPA). Plead UCL fraudulent prong independently based on the reasonable-consumer deception. Plead UCL unfair prong based on the systematic consumer harm outweighing any legitimate business interest.

damages_mosaic.note: UCL alone does not yield large monetary recovery. The damages mosaic for auto fraud cases:
damages_mosaic.ucl_restitution: All payments made under fraud / void contracts (Korea Supply bounded restitution)
damages_mosaic.clra_actual_damages: Compensatory damages under §1780(a) for CLRA violations
damages_mosaic.civ_1709_deceit: Out-of-pocket damages under common-law deceit (forthcoming standard)
damages_mosaic.civ_3294_punitive: Punitive damages for fraud with clear and convincing evidence

operational_notes_for_steward_cases.federal_court_strategy: For FCRA-based UCL unlawful prong claims: consider filing in California state court to avoid Spokeo/TransUnion standing barrier. FCRA violation borrowed into UCL unlawful prong = UCL claim in state court where Article III standing requirements do not apply.
